questions.explanation: Ransomware encrypts files (or entire systems) and presents a ransom demand for the decryption key, combining cryptography with extortion.

questions.stem: Rootkits are particularly dangerous because they:

choices.A: Spread via email to all contacts
choices.B: Modify OS components at a low level to hide themselves and other malware from detection

questions.explanation: Rootkits operate at the kernel level, modifying OS APIs to make themselves and other malware invisible to the OS and security tools.

choices.C: A new user account was created

questions.explanation: 4624=Successful Logon, 4625=Failed Logon, 4720=User Account Created, 4688=New Process Created. These are critical SOC monitoring events.

questions.stem: A scheduled task named 'WindowsUpdateService' running base64-encoded PowerShell should prompt:

choices.C: Immediate investigation, malware uses plausible names and encoded payloads to establish persistence

questions.explanation: Attackers name malicious tasks after legitimate Windows components (MITRE T1036) and encode payloads to evade detection. Any encoded payload in an unexpected task is high priority.

choices.A: Initial access through phishing or exploitation
choices.D: Techniques attackers use to maintain access across reboots and credential changes

questions.explanation: Persistence techniques (scheduled tasks, registry run keys, startup folders, services) ensure attackers maintain a foothold even after system restart.

questions.stem: Fileless malware is difficult to detect because:

choices.A: It operates in memory and uses legitimate OS tools, leaving no malware files for antivirus to scan
choices.B: It uses unbreakable encryption to hide on disk
choices.C: It only activates at specific times
choices.D: It targets firmware below the OS layer

questions.explanation: Fileless malware lives in memory and abuses built-in tools (PowerShell, WMI, LOLBins). No malicious file is written to disk, bypassing file-based AV detection.

questions.stem: The MITRE ATT&CK framework is best described as:

choices.A: A knowledge base of real adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures based on observed attacks
choices.B: A vulnerability scoring system for CVEs
choices.C: A compliance framework for government systems

questions.explanation: MITRE ATT&CK documents real adversary behaviours across the attack lifecycle, enabling defenders to map detections and identify coverage gaps.

questions.stem: The immediate containment action when ransomware is confirmed active is:

choices.A: Back up remaining unencrypted files to an external drive
choices.B: Immediately disconnect the device from the network to stop encryption spreading to shared drives
choices.C: Run a full antivirus scan to identify and remove the ransomware
choices.D: Pay the ransom before more files are encrypted

questions.explanation: Network isolation is the highest-priority containment action. Disconnecting within seconds can prevent ransomware from spreading to network shares.

choices.A: Known software vulnerabilities with CVE identifiers
choices.C: Forensic artefacts suggesting a system may be compromised, unusual processes, connections, or new accounts
choices.D: Configuration deviations from a security baseline

questions.explanation: IoCs are evidence of potential compromise: unknown processes, unusual outbound connections, suspicious scheduled tasks, or new admin accounts.
